Master’s degree in learning disabilities, special education, education, psychology, speech language pathology, communication disorders, educational or school psychology, counseling, or rehabilitation counseling AND 15 semester units of upper division or graduate study in the area of learning disabilities, to include, adult cognitive and achievement assessment or the equivalent. **The incumbent must be certified through the California Community College Chancelors Office (CCCCO) as a Learning Disability Specialist. Experience: Experience that indicates a sensitivity to and an understanding of the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, disability, and ethnic backgrounds of community college students, including those with physical and learning disabilities. The incumbent must possess the minimum experience for certification as a CCCCO approved Learning Disability Specialist. Experience conducting evaluations of Community College Students for Disabled Students Program and Services (DSPS) eligibility. Desired Qualifications: Counseling experience at a community college or high school level specifically providing services to students with disabilities.
